clue.text: Frustrated aims of one supplying hoods

indicators.note: aims that are frustrated are thwarted and thrown into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone's plans are thwarted while they provide head coverings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frustrated' rearranges AIMS, OF and I (one). 'Hoods' means gangsters, not head coverings; 'supplying' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoods is slang for gangsters, and Sicilian-American mobsters are the classic example.

clue.text: A way of being an old teenager at end of line

parts.note: a Mod was a 1960s British teenage stylist on a scooter

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of the word line

explanation.surface: Life as a former adolescent, at the finish of a row.
explanation.walkthrough: Mods were a 1960s British youth movement of sharp-suited scooter riders.
explanation.definitionFit: A mode is a manner or method, a particular way of existing or doing something.

clue.text: 9 since died

parts.note: for can mean since or because, as in 'for it was late'
d is the standard abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A cross-reference followed by a note that someone has passed away.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 refers to the answer at 9 across, a film-maker; John Ford made classic Westerns.
explanation.definitionFit: John Ford was a celebrated American film director known for Westerns such as The Searchers.

clue.text: Butcher's former sexual partner left out

parts.note: once means formerly, at a former time

indicators.note: out tells us that the letter for left is removed from the partner word

parts.note: a lover is a sexual partner

explanation.surface: A meat seller's ex-lover has been excluded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butcher's' is Cockney rhyming slang: butcher's hook = look. Take L (left) out of LOVER to leave OVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhyming slang for a quick look, which is what a cursory inspection or glance amounts to.

clue.text: Woman takes duck on river to be a 9

indicators.note: takes means the woman's name holds the following pieces inside it

parts.note: Ivy is a woman's name
a duck in cricket is a score of nought, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A woman picks up a duck by the water in order to become a film-maker.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a cricket score of zero, hence O; O placed on R (down clue) goes inside IVY.
explanation.definitionFit: James Ivory is the American film director of the Merchant Ivory partnership, known for A Room with a View.

clue.text: 9 bears flowers

definitions.meaning: a film-maker, Mel ... of Blazing Saddles
to brook something is to tolerate or bear it, so this is the verb in the third person
things that flow, here small streams or rivulets

explanation.surface: A film-maker puts up with blooms.
explanation.walkthrough: A triple definition. 'Flowers' is read as 'things that flow', not blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Mel Brooks directs films; brooks means tolerates; brooks are streams, which flow.

clue.text: Small house, end of terrace, without a certain something — move elsewhere

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so these letters go around another piece

parts.note: res is short for residence, a house in estate-agent shorthand

indicators.note: end of selects the final letter of the word terrace

parts.note: it means sex appeal or that indefinable quality, a certain something

explanation.surface: An estate agent describes a little end-terrace house lacking charm before relocating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking; the surface reads like an estate agent's listing.
explanation.definitionFit: To resite is to put something in a new location, relocating it elsewhere.

clue.text: Chimp loath to get hit about the eye

indicators.note: getting hit knocks the letters of the two words about into a new order

explanation.surface: An ape is unwilling to be struck near its eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get hit' rearranges the ten letters of CHIMP and LOATH; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means relating to or concerning the eye, as in an eye surgeon's specialism.

clue.text: Out of touch with reality when reacting to a blow on the head?

definitions.text: when reacting to a blow on the head?
definitions.meaning: cartoon characters struck on the head see stars circling before their eyes

explanation.surface: Someone so naive they seem to have been knocked on the head.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is whimsical: after a blow you literally see stars.
explanation.definitionFit: Naively idealistic people are said to have stars in their eyes; literally, concussion makes you see stars.

clue.text: Awful time to plug Gordon Bennett, governor!

parts.note: dire means dreadful or awful

indicators.note: plugging means filling a gap, so one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: a British exclamation of surprise, like 'Cor!'

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a dreadful time spent advertising, addressed to a boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gordon Bennett!' and 'Cor!' are both British exclamations of surprise; T goes inside COR to give CTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A director, like a governor, is someone who controls or manages an organisation.

clue.text: No jolly wheeze like the endless conjoining with young woman I'd abandoned

parts.note: as means like, in the manner of

indicators.note: endless says the word the loses its final letter
abandoned means the letters of I'd are dropped from the young woman

parts.note: a maid is a young woman

explanation.surface: A joyless prank involving a girl who has left her past behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims THE to TH; 'abandoned' removes ID from MAID, leaving MA. A 'wheeze' is a prank, but here literal wheezing.
explanation.definitionFit: The condition causes laboured wheezing breaths, which are anything but a jolly joke or prank.

clue.text: Really absorbed by a piece of information

parts.note: being absorbed by something is being in it
a fact is a single item of information

explanation.surface: Someone engrossed in a single item of knowledge.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are adverbial phrases meaning actually or truly, used for emphasis.

clue.text: Corporation grasping type whose victims will be cut up

definitions.text: whose victims will be cut up
definitions.note: the definition stands for a noun, one whose victims will be cut up, so 'one' is understood

parts.note: a corporation is a body, an organised group
someone grasping grabs things, a snatcher

explanation.surface: A greedy firm whose prey ends up dismembered.
explanation.walkthrough: Historically grave robbers sold corpses to anatomists for dissection, hence the victims being cut up.
explanation.definitionFit: Resurrection men dug up corpses so that anatomy schools could dissect them.

clue.text: Disillusioned with Gordian intricacy and driving in the rough

parts.note: to go off something is to become disillusioned with it

indicators.note: intricacy suggests a knotted, tangled arrangement, so the letters are muddled

explanation.surface: Someone fed up with the complexity of the famous knot.
explanation.walkthrough: The Gordian knot was proverbially intricate; here 'intricacy' tangles GORDIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Driving vehicles over rough terrain away from paved roads describes this activity.

clue.text: No traveller at sea tangled with myth about love

indicators.note: about places these letters around another piece
tangled means mixed up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A sailor lost on the ocean becomes entangled in legend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' looks like an anagram signal but is fodder; 'tangled' rearranges AT SEA and MYTH around O.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who prefers to remain at home is the opposite of a traveller.

clue.text: Time to honour the old man of Hayes' draft constitution

definitions.text: Time to honour the old man

indicators.note: a constitution is a make-up, so the letters are composed anew

explanation.surface: A man named Hayes drafts a constitution and looks back on his father.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constitution' rearranges HAYES and DRAFT; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The annual day in June celebrates fathers, informally called the old man.

clue.text: Cut down bust, "Chesty"!

indicators.note: bust means broken, so the letters are smashed and rearranged

explanation.surface: A sculpture of a buxom figure gets reduced in size.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bust' looks like a chest, matching 'Chesty', but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to mow or cut down grass or crops with a long curved blade.

clue.text: Kay's dumped by artist for 9

indicators.note: dumped by says the letter is thrown out of the painter

parts.note: Paul Klee was a Swiss-German painter
Kay is the spelling of the letter K

explanation.surface: A woman named Kay is ditched by a painter in favour of a film-maker.
explanation.walkthrough: Kay is not a woman but the letter K, dropped from KLEE; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Spike Lee and Ang Lee are both well-known film directors.

clue.text: Intended needs to be outside right church for 9

indicators.note: the intended word goes around the next two pieces

parts.note: meant means intended

explanation.surface: A fiance must stay outside the right-wing church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intended' looks like a noun for a fiance, but it works here as the past participle.
explanation.definitionFit: Ismail Merchant produced films and directed some, as half of Merchant Ivory.

clue.text: Colourless American takes top off 9

indicators.note: taking the top off drops the first letter

parts.note: gray is the American spelling of grey, a colourless shade

explanation.surface: A dull US citizen removes his hat in front of a film-maker.
explanation.walkthrough: Satyajit Ray was the great Bengali film director.
explanation.definitionFit: Satyajit Ray was an acclaimed Indian film director, maker of the Apu trilogy.

clue.text: Put together said evil article on weak glue

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the sound of the word counts, not its spelling

parts.note: sin is evil, wrongdoing
the is the definite article
size is a thin gelatinous glue used on paper and plaster

explanation.surface: A wicked newspaper piece is written on flimsy adhesive.
explanation.walkthrough: Only 'evil' is spoken: SIN gives the sound SYN. 'Size' is a thin glue used to seal walls.
explanation.definitionFit: To synthesise is to combine elements into a whole, to put them together.

clue.text: Sutherland encircles Highway 9

indicators.note: encircles means goes round another piece

parts.note: Joan Sutherland was the Australian soprano
RD is short for road, a highway

explanation.surface: A Scottish county surrounds a main road.
explanation.walkthrough: Sutherland looks like the Scottish county, but it is the opera singer Joan Sutherland.
explanation.definitionFit: Neil Jordan is the Irish film director of The Crying Game.

clue.text: Sophistry refined and internalised by Bill Gates finally becomes science

indicators.note: internalised by means put inside another piece

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill

indicators.note: refined means reworked, so the letters are rearranged
finally picks the last letter of the word Gates

explanation.surface: Clever argument polished by a tech billionaire turns into hard science.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface wants 'Bill Gates' to be the Microsoft founder; the name splits into two separate pieces instead.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the branch of science applying physics to stars and other celestial bodies.

clue.text: 9 square pitch

definitions.meaning: a squared paving block, a sett

explanation.surface: A film-maker on a square playing field.
explanation.walkthrough: A double definition; 'pitch' is a paving of laid blocks, not a sports field.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver Stone directs films; a squared block of rock laid in paving is a stone.

clue.text: Guardian's reported 9

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: the Guardian newspaper speaks of itself as 'we', so the Guardian's is 'we are', contracted

explanation.surface: The newspaper's coverage of a film-maker.
explanation.walkthrough: Newspapers refer to themselves as 'we', so the Guardian is = we're, said aloud to give the director.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Weir is the Australian film director of The Truman Show.

clue.text: Buck up, 9?

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a buck is a male deer

explanation.surface: Cheer up, film-maker?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buck up' reads as 'cheer up', but Buck is a deer, turned upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Carol Reed was the British director of The Third Man.

clue.text: Medieval lover has celebrated many a birthday with an amphetamine

parts.note: someone who has had many birthdays is old
E is ecstasy, an amphetamine-based drug

explanation.surface: An aged romantic from the Middle Ages takes a party drug.
explanation.walkthrough: Isolde is the heroine of the medieval romance Tristan and Isolde.
explanation.definitionFit: Isolde is the beloved of Tristan in the medieval Arthurian romance.

clue.text: Vase shattered with Cleo's improvised jazz singing

indicators.note: a shattered vase is broken to pieces, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive adds no letter to Cleo

explanation.surface: A singer called Cleo breaks a pot while scat singing.
explanation.walkthrough: Cleo Laine is a famous British jazz singer, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: This jazz style sets lyrics to instrumental solos, a form of jazz singing.

clue.text: Looks like a seasick sailor's means of preventing scurvy?

definitions.meaning: a seasick sailor is pale green, so the phrase means 'is green'
leafy vegetables rich in vitamin C ward off scurvy

explanation.surface: A nauseous seaman's complexion and his diet against scurvy.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition reads 'green is', the 's' as a contraction.
explanation.definitionFit: Green vegetables supply vitamin C, and a seasick face looks green.

clue.text: Close-bound sickly tree logged

indicators.note: bound means tied round, so this piece encloses another

parts.note: close means end, a conclusion

indicators.note: a sickly tree is in poor shape, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An unhealthy tree tightly bound has been felled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Logged' suggests felled timber, but it means recorded; 'Close-bound' reads as one word but splits into piece and indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Logged means recorded or written into a record, like entering in a log.
